deep.reconstruction:
Context. Folios 24r–26r belong to Gauss's unpublished work on biquadratic (quartic) residues in the Gaussian integers. Two complex moduli are in play, written with components a, b and A, B (presumably m = a+bi, M = A+Bi). The previous page gives the change of variables y0 = -b t + a u, X0 = -A t - B u. Its inverse is α t = -B y0 - a X0, α u = A y0 - b X0. Inverting fixes α = aA + bB = Re(m·conj(M)); this is my deduction. The page also uses a second constant written 𝔟 (fraktur b). It is presumably the 'imaginary' companion ±(aB − bA); I could not confirm this from the page.

The character ε = ±1 attached to each term t+ui is a quartic Gauss-lemma-type sign. On the previous page Gauss sorted the terms into complexes θ'' and θ''' and stated ε-rules depending on divisibility by 1+i. This page states the rule 'after the above correction' (Nach obiger Verbesserung).

Step 1 – the four complexes. Each is the set of Gaussian integers T+Ui lying in a half-open parallelogram, written as two linear forms required to be positive and less than ½𝔟 or ½α. This follows the explicit 'beide positiv und < ½α' of the previous page.
• Θ: bT − aU > 0 and −BT + AU > 0, bound ½𝔟.
• Θ': −bT + aU > 0 and AT + BU > 0, bound ½α.
• Θ'': −bT + aU > 0 and −BT + AU > 0, bound ½𝔟.
• Θ''': bT − aU > 0 and AT + BU > 0, bound ½α.
This applies 'insofern resp. 𝔟 oder α positiv', i.e. assuming 𝔟 > 0 (for Θ, Θ'') and α > 0 (for Θ', Θ''').

The first form is always ±(bT − aU), which is the 'imaginary' coordinate with respect to m. The second form is either the corresponding coordinate with respect to M or its 'real' coordinate. The four parallelograms are therefore the quarter-systems adjacent to one another, as in the sketch.

Step 2 – the sign rule. A Gaussian integer T+Ui is divisible by 1+i exactly when T+U is even. For such elements:
• ε = +1 on Θ (if 𝔟 > 0);
• ε = −1 on Θ' (if α > 0);
• ε = −1 on Θ'' (if 𝔟 > 0);
• ε = +1 on Θ''' (if α > 0).
Implicitly, and confirmed by the examples, the elements not divisible by 1+i get the opposite sign.

Step 3 – worked example. Parameters are not stated on the page.
• Θ = {−i, −2i, −3i, 1−i, 1−2i, 1−3i} with ε = −1, +1, −1, +1, −1, +1.
• Θ' = {2−i, 3−i} with ε = +1, −1.
• Θ'' = {1, 1+i, 1+2i} with ε = +1, −1, +1.
• Θ''' = {−1, −2} with ε = −1, +1.
In each case ε = +1 or −1 exactly according to the parity of T+U, with the sign the table prescribes.

Step 4 – link to the neighbouring pages. The previous page's 4th-class terms reappear here up to sign: −1 (ε −1) and 2−i (ε +1). The 3rd-class terms +2 and −3+i (ε +1, −1) reappear as −2 ∈ Θ''' and 3−i ∈ Θ'. The ε-sums over the complexes are 0, 0, 1, 0. These are exactly the values 4Θ = 0, 4Θ' = 0, 4Θ'' = 4, 4Θ''' = 0 computed on the next page. There Θ denotes the ε-sum over the complex, to be evaluated from 'Vorschriften' II–V plus sign-corrections R.

Step 5 – the figure. It draws the integer lattice with the four parallelograms Θ'', Θ, Θ', Θ''' sketched. Points are marked by dots, circles and stars; presumably these distinguish divisible from non-divisible elements and boundary/corner points.

Purpose. This is a lattice-point (Gauss-lemma / Eisenstein-type) evaluation of a quartic character as a signed count over a quarter-system, in service of a proof of the biquadratic reciprocity law.
errors: No arithmetic error is detectable: every example entry obeys the stated parity rule, and the ε-sums agree with the next page.

The page is elliptic. The upper bound '< ½𝔟' / '< ½α' is written once per line; following the previous page I take it to apply to both linear forms. The rule for elements not divisible by 1+i is left implicit and is only inferable from the examples.

I could not reconstruct parameters a, b, A, B for which the listed sets are exactly the lattice points of the stated parallelograms. Trial values contradicted either the sign conditions or the bounds. Either the example parameters lie on another page, or the inequalities (bounds/strictness) are not to be read literally. Exact membership in the example is therefore unverified.

results.what: Partition of the relevant Gaussian integers into four adjacent half-open parallelograms Θ, Θ', Θ'', Θ''' defined by linear forms in (T,U) built from the components of two moduli, bounded by ½α or ½𝔟
results.modern_name: Quarter-system (Gaussian-integer analogue of the half-system in Gauss's lemma); lattice-point region decomposition
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss's lemma (1808) for the quadratic case; quartic analogues usually attributed to Eisenstein (1844) and later writers

results.what: Sign rule: ε = ±1 according to divisibility of T+Ui by 1+i (parity of T+U), with the sign depending on the complex and on the signs of α, 𝔟
results.modern_name: Quartic Gauss-lemma-type evaluation of the biquadratic residue character via a signed lattice-point count
results.usually_credited_to: Eisenstein (lattice/lemma proofs of biquadratic reciprocity, 1844); Gauss is known to have possessed an unpublished proof

results.what: Numerical check: ε-sums over the four complexes are 0, 0, 1, 0, matching 4Θ = 0, 4Θ' = 0, 4Θ'' = 4, 4Θ''' = 0 on the next page
results.modern_name: Numerical verification of a character-sum formula

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss is well known to have worked on biquadratic reciprocity and claimed a proof; parts of his Nachlass on it are printed in Werke II and have been discussed. A detailed lattice-point/Gauss-lemma style apparatus with parity-of-(1+i) sign rules is a notable unpublished technical detail. It anticipates Eisenstein-type arguments, but it is not a new major result unknown to be his.

checkable.asserts: The inversion formulas of the previous page hold with α = aA + bB.

checkable.asserts: T+Ui is divisible by 1+i iff T+U is even.
In Θ, ε = +1 for elements divisible by 1+i and −1 otherwise.
In Θ', ε = −1 for elements divisible by 1+i and +1 otherwise.
In Θ'', ε = −1 for elements divisible by 1+i and +1 otherwise.
In Θ''', ε = +1 for elements divisible by 1+i and −1 otherwise.
The ε-sums give 4Θ = 0, 4Θ' = 0, 4Θ'' = 4, 4Θ''' = 0, as on the next page.
